base-convert.title: Base Conversion Tool
base-convert.intro: A base conversion tool that instantly converts between binary, octal, decimal and hexadecimal, with real-time results and automatic detection of 0b/0o/0x prefixes
base-convert.problem1: Base conversion is a common need in programming and computer operations, but doing it manually is error-prone and inefficient.
base-convert.problem2: Numbers are represented quite differently across bases, and developers frequently need to switch between binary, octal, decimal and hexadecimal.
base-convert.problem3: Understanding and converting numbers across different bases is a challenge for non-professionals.
base-convert.formatBin: Binary (BIN): Contains only digits 0 and 1, supports the 0b prefix.
base-convert.formatDec: Decimal (DEC): Contains digits 0-9, the most commonly used base in everyday life.
base-convert.formatHex: Hexadecimal (HEX): Contains digits 0-9 and letters A-F (case-insensitive), supports the 0x prefix.
base-convert.featureRealTime: Real-time conversion: Results in all bases appear immediately as you type, with no manual triggering required.
base-convert.featureCopy: One-click copy: Copy the result of a single base, or copy all results at once.
base-convert.featurePreset: Presets: Quick input of common values for convenient testing and learning.
base-convert.featureAutoDetect: Auto detection: Intelligently recognizes base prefixes and automatically switches to the matching input mode.
base-convert.usageSelectBase: Select the source base: Click the base tabs above (BIN/OCT/DEC/HEX) to choose the base of the number you enter.
base-convert.usageInputNumber: Enter a number: Type the number to convert into the input box, and it will be converted in real time automatically.
base-convert.usageViewResult: View results: The result is shown simultaneously in four formats: binary, octal, decimal and hexadecimal.
base-convert.usageCopyResult: Copy results: Click the "Copy" button next to each result to copy that base's value individually, or click "Copy All" to copy all results at once.
base-convert.usagePreset: Use presets: Click a preset tag below (e.g., 255, 1024, 0xFF) to quickly fill in common values for conversion.
base-convert.formatDetailHex: Hexadecimal (HEX): Contains digits 0-9 and letters A-F (case-insensitive), e.g., FF.
base-convert.shortcutEnter: Press Enter to trigger the conversion.
base-convert.shortcutSwitch: When you switch bases, the current input value is automatically converted to the new base's representation.
base-convert.formatRule1: The number entered must comply with the format rules of the selected base, otherwise an error will be shown.
base-convert.formatRule2: Binary allows only 0 and 1; octal allows only 0-7; decimal allows only 0-9; hexadecimal allows 0-9 and A-F.
base-convert.formatRule3: The number must not contain spaces, commas or other separators.
base-convert.range1: The supported value range is -2^53 ~ 2^53 (JavaScript's safe integer range).
base-convert.range2: Very large numbers beyond the safe range may lose precision.
base-convert.range3: For negative numbers, the hexadecimal result is displayed as a minus sign followed by the hexadecimal representation of the absolute value.
base-convert.security1: All conversions run entirely in your local browser; no data is uploaded to any server.
base-convert.security2: Avoid processing values containing sensitive information on public devices.
base-convert.faqConvertError: Conversion error: Check that the input complies with the format rules of the selected base.
base-convert.faqValueAbnormal: Abnormal value: Extremely large numbers may exceed JavaScript's safe integer range; consider processing them in segments.
base-convert.faqCopyFailed: Copy failed: Check that your browser allows clipboard access.
base-convert.msgInvalidNumber: Cannot parse as a valid number

regex.desc: An online regex testing tool for testing and validating regular expressions, with real-time matching and replacement, and support for multiple regex flavors
regex.flagsHint: Flags: g Global  i Case-insensitive  m Multiline  s Dot matches newline  u Unicode
regex.presetsTitle: Common Regex Cheat Sheet (Click to Fill)
regex.problem1: Test and validate regular expressions with real-time matching and replacement.
regex.problem2: Simplify tedious manual operations, improving work efficiency and accuracy.
regex.problem3: Use it online anytime, anywhere, without installing professional software.
regex.formatRegex: Regular Expression: Full processing support for this format.
regex.formatJs: JavaScript: Full processing support for this format.
regex.formatPython: Python: Full processing support for this format.
regex.featureOnline: Online Processing: All operations run in your browser; no downloads or installation required.
regex.featurePreview: Real-time Preview: Results are displayed instantly for easy adjustment and confirmation.
regex.featureExport: One-click Export: Quickly export processed files or copy results.
regex.featureSecurity: Data Security: All data is processed locally and never uploaded to any server.
regex.guideInputRegex: Enter a regex pattern: Type the pattern you want to test in the regex input box, e.g. \d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}.
regex.guideSelectFlags: Select flags: Click the flag buttons to set regex flags (g: global match, i: case-insensitive, m: multiline mode, s: dot matches newline, u: Unicode).
regex.guideInputText: Enter test text: Enter the text to match in the test text area.
regex.guideRealtime: Real-time matching: The system displays matching results in real time and highlights all matches.
regex.guideDetails: View match details: See detailed information for each match in the list below, including position, length, and capture groups.
regex.guideLocate: Locate a match: Click the "Locate" button to jump to the highlighted position of the corresponding match.
regex.guideSwitchReplace: Switch to Replace: Click the "Replace" tab to switch to replacement mode.
regex.guideSetRegex: Enter a regex pattern: Set the pattern to match.
regex.guideInputSource: Enter original text: Enter the content to replace in the original text area.
regex.guideSetReplace: Set replacement content: Enter the replacement content in the "Replace With" input box, supporting capture group references like $1, $2.
regex.guideDoReplace: Run the replacement: Click the "Replace" button or wait for the automatic replacement.
regex.guideClickPreset: Click a preset: Click a preset regex below to fill it in quickly.
regex.guidePresetContent: Preset content: Includes common regexes for dates, phone numbers, emails, URLs, IP addresses, ID card numbers, Chinese characters, blank lines, HTML tags, hex colors, numbers, words, and more.
regex.syntaxCharClass: Character classes: . matches any character, \d matches a digit, \w matches a letter, digit, or underscore, \s matches whitespace.
regex.syntaxQuantifier: Quantifiers: * zero or more, + one or more, ? zero or one, {n} exactly n, {n,m} between n and m.
regex.syntaxAnchor: Anchors: ^ start of line, $ end of line, \b word boundary.
regex.syntaxCharSet: Character sets: [abc] matches a, b, or c; [^abc] matches any character except a, b, and c.
regex.notesEscape: Special characters must be escaped, such as \, ., *, +, ?, (), [], {}, ^, $, |.
regex.notesDoubleEscape: In JavaScript regexes, backslashes need double escaping, e.g. \\d.
regex.notesGroupNumbering: Capture groups are numbered starting from $1; $0 represents the full match.
regex.flagGlobal: g (Global): Find all matches instead of only the first one.
regex.flagInsensitive: i (Case-insensitive): Match without distinguishing uppercase and lowercase.
regex.flagMultiline: m (Multiline): ^ and $ match the start and end of every line.
regex.flagDotAll: s (Dot matches newline): . can match line break characters.
regex.perfComplex: Complex regex patterns may cause performance issues, especially when processing large amounts of text.
regex.perfGreedy: Avoid greedy quantifiers (*, +); consider using lazy quantifiers (*?, +?).
regex.perfLargeText: Testing very large text (over 100KB) may cause the browser to lag.
regex.securityLocal: All processing is done locally in your browser; data is never uploaded to any server.
regex.securityPublicDevice: It is recommended not to process text containing sensitive information on public devices.
regex.faqSyntax: Syntax error: Check whether special characters in the regex pattern are escaped correctly.
regex.faqNoMatch: No matches: Verify the pattern and test text are correct, and check the flag settings.
regex.faqPartialMatch: Incomplete matches: Make sure the g (global) flag is enabled.
regex.faqReplaceIssue: Replacement issues: Check whether the capture group references in the replacement content are correct.
regex.msgInputRequired: Please enter a regex pattern and text

cron.title: Cron Expression Parser
cron.intro: A Cron expression parser supporting both 5-field and 6-field formats, providing expression parsing, generation, and next-execution-time prediction
cron.specialCharLegend: * Any value  , List  - Range  / Step  ? No specific value  L Last  W Nearest weekday  # Nth weekday of month
cron.problem1: Cron expressions are the core syntax for scheduled task management, but the 5-field or 6-field time combinations are hard for beginners to understand and write.
cron.problem2: Manually calculating Cron execution times is tedious and error-prone, especially with complex step and range expressions.
cron.problem3: Different schedulers (such as Linux Cron, Spring Scheduler, and Quartz) interpret Cron expressions slightly differently, which can easily cause confusion.
cron.formatStandard5: 5-field Standard Format: Minute Hour Day Month Weekday, compatible with most standard Cron schedulers.
cron.formatExtended6: 6-field Extended Format: Second Minute Hour Day Month Weekday, for schedulers with second-level precision (e.g., Quartz, Spring).
cron.formatSpecialChars: Special Characters: Supports all standard Cron special characters such as * (any), , (list), - (range), / (step), ? (no specific value), and L (last).
cron.featureParse: Expression Parsing: Converts Cron expressions into human-readable descriptions at a glance.
cron.featureGenerate: Expression Generation: Configure the rules for each field through a visual interface and auto-generate the corresponding Cron expression.
cron.featurePredict: Execution Time Prediction: Calculates the next 10 execution times based on the current time to help you plan task schedules.
cron.featureFormatSwitch: Format Switching: Quickly switch between 5-field and 6-field formats, automatically adding or removing the seconds field.
cron.usageInput: Enter Expression: Type a 5-field or 6-field Cron expression in the input box, e.g., */5 * * * * or 0 */5 * * * *.
cron.usageAutoParse: Automatic Parsing: The expression is parsed automatically as you type, with the visualization and execution-time prediction updating in real time.
cron.usageVisual: Visual Display: The parsing result shows the meaning of each field (second, minute, hour, day, month, weekday) as cards.
cron.usageExecTime: View Execution Times: The tool predicts a list of upcoming execution times so you can understand the task schedule.
cron.usagePresets: Use Presets: Click a preset button below (e.g., every minute, every hour, every day) to quickly fill in common expressions.
cron.usageGenMode: Select Generation Mode: Switch to the "Generate Cron" tab and configure the execution rules for each field through the visual interface.
cron.usageGenFormat: Format Switching: Click the "5-field" or "6-field (with seconds)" button to switch the generation format.
cron.usageGenSecond: Second Config: In 6-field format, supports four modes: every second, every N seconds, range, and specific values.
cron.usageGenMinute: Minute Config: Supports four modes: every minute, every N minutes, range, and specific values.
cron.usageGenHour: Hour Config: Supports four modes: every hour, every N hours, range, and specific values.
cron.usageGenDay: Day Config: Supports every day or specific dates.
cron.usageGenMonth: Month Config: Supports every month or specific months.
cron.usageGenWeekday: Weekday Config: Supports any weekday or specific weekdays.
cron.usageGenResult: View Result: The corresponding Cron expression and description are generated automatically after configuration.
cron.usageFmt5: 5-field Format: Minute Hour Day Month Weekday
cron.usageFmt6: 6-field Format: Second Minute Hour Day Month Weekday
cron.usageFmtSecond: Second (0-59): Specifies the second of the minute when the task runs (6-field format only).
cron.usageFmtMinute: Minute (0-59): Specifies the minute of the hour when the task runs.
cron.usageFmtHour: Hour (0-23): Specifies the hour of the day when the task runs.
cron.usageFmtDay: Day (1-31): Specifies the day of the month when the task runs.
cron.usageFmtMonth: Month (1-12): Specifies the month of the year when the task runs.
cron.usageFmtWeekday: Weekday (0-6): Specifies the weekday when the task runs (0=Sunday).
cron.scAsterisk: *: Any value, meaning all possible values for that field.
cron.scQuestion: ?: No specific value, usually used for the day and weekday fields when they conflict.
cron.scL: L: Last, e.g., L in the day field means the last day of the month.
cron.noteFormat1: A Cron expression must be in 5-field or 6-field format, with fields separated by spaces.
cron.noteFormat2: Each field's value must be within its valid range; out-of-range values will cause parsing to fail.
cron.noteFormat3: In the weekday field, 0 means Sunday and 1-6 mean Monday through Saturday.
cron.notePredict1: Execution time prediction is based on the current time and is for reference only.
cron.notePredict2: Actual execution times may be affected by the system timezone and the task scheduler.
cron.notePredict3: The 6-field format supports second-level execution time calculation.
cron.noteSecurity1: All processing is done in your local browser; data is never uploaded to any server.
cron.noteSecurity2: Avoid processing Cron expressions containing sensitive information on shared or public devices.
cron.faqParseFail: Parsing Failed: Check whether the Cron expression format is correct and the field values are within valid ranges.
cron.faqExecTime: Abnormal Execution Times: Verify that the timezone setting is correct; some schedulers may use a different timezone.
cron.faqCopyFail: Copy Failed: Check whether the browser allows clipboard access.
cron.faqNoChange: No Change After Format Switch: Make sure you enter an expression in the Parse tab before switching formats.

file-size.standardDesc: IEC: 1 KB = 1024 B (OS standard); SI: 1 KB = 1000 B (disk manufacturer standard)

file-size.unitMb: Megabyte (MB): Common for images and music files.
file-size.unitGb: Gigabyte (GB): Common for videos and system images.
file-size.unitTb: Terabyte (TB): Common for hard drive capacity.
file-size.featureRealtime: Real-time Conversion: Instantly shows all unit results as you type, no button click needed.

file-size.notesDiffTitle: 1. Why Does My Hard Drive Show Less Capacity Than Advertised?
file-size.noteDiff: Hard drive manufacturers use SI standard (1000-based), while operating systems use IEC standard (1024-based). For example, a 500GB drive: manufacturer calculates 500×1000³, system displays ÷1024³ ≈ 465 GiB. This is normal, not a quality issue.
file-size.notePrecision: Results are displayed with up to 6 significant digits. Very small or very large values may have minor floating-point precision differences.
